text:
B: Hello. Can you hear me alright?
A: Yeah. Hi. I'm Kirsty.
B: Kulwinder. Hello.
A: Hello.
B: So. Where are you?
A: Burnley. In Lancashire.
B: I'm in Hayes. West London. Do you work?
A: Erm, not at the minute. I got made redundant from a factory. Fourteen months ago now.
B: Mm. I'm not working either. My hands. I was a tailor.
A: Oh. Sorry. That must be hard, if it's your hands.
B: It is. It was what I did, you know? Twenty years. Now I do hems for the family and that's it. Are you on Universal Credit, then?
A: Yeah. Erm, is that okay to say on here?
B: Why not? It's not a crime. I've done all the forms myself, for years. The council, the benefits, all of it. The trick is you keep copies of everything. Every letter, every phone call, you write the date and the name of who you spoke to. Because they lose things, and then it's your word against theirs.
A: I don't do that. I should. I just sort of dread it. The appointments especially.
B: The Jobcentre?
A: Yeah. I go over what I'm going to say on the bus, and then I get there and I forget it all.
B: Write it down. Take the paper in. They don't mind. I used to take my notebook to every job, at the shop, every customer, what they wanted, the measurements. Nobody could argue with me.
A: That's a good idea, actually. A notebook.
B: Is this how you make money as well, these studies?
A: A bit, yeah. Just for extras. Cat food, mainly.
B: Same. Not the cat food. I do surveys on my phone in the evening. Some of them are stupid. Twenty minutes about crisps.
A: I had one about toothpaste. It went on forever.
B: Ha. Haan, those ones. Do you live with family?
A: No, on my own. Me mam's ten minutes away, though. I take her flapjacks.
B: My mum's ten minutes too. She comes every day. She'd love someone bringing her flapjacks, she'd stop complaining for once.
A: Mine still complains. She says they're too chewy.
B: They're supposed to be chewy.
A: That's what I said. Erm, do you still sew, for yourself?
B: Little bits. Curtains last month, for my daughter's room. It took me a week instead of a day. I had to stop every hour, my fingers lock up. Before, I'd have done it in an afternoon and had dinner on as well.
A: But you still did it.
B: Yes. I suppose I did. They're good curtains.
A: I bet they're really neat.
B: The hems are perfect. Nobody notices but me.
A: I'm like that with drawing. I'll rub out one line about fifty times. Nobody else would know it was wrong.
B: You draw? What do you—
